analysis.title: Strong jobs data put a December Fed hike in play
key_insights: October payrolls rose 165,000 against consensus near 65,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1% and prior months were revised higher.
Markets now price a December Fed rate hike after the payrolls report and calls from several Fed officials for a more restrictive stance.
Nuveen expects one more Fed hike by year-end, likely in December, followed by an extended hold through 2027. The path depends on the energy shock and its pass-through to core inflation.
Nuveen forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% for year-end 2026 and 4.75% for year-end 2027. It forecasts the 2-year at 4.70% this year and 4.50% next year.
With the 10-year at 4.86% after four weeks of rally, Nuveen sees modest room for yields to rise into December.
Treasury yields fell for a fourth straight week as investors sought safety after the election. Short and intermediate yields fell most, so the curve shape barely changed.

Municipals led all sectors for a fourth straight week. The Bloomberg Municipal Index returned +0.92% and yields 4.09%. Nuveen prefers longer-duration municipals over Treasuries and would add high-quality duration on dips.
Taxable municipals returned +0.47% with spreads at 56 bps and yields near 5.51%, which Nuveen says attract crossover investors.

Investment grade corporates finished roughly flat in price despite heavy issuance from large technology and AI-linked companies. Fund inflows jumped well above the four-week average. The index returned +0.41% with spreads at 91 bps.

High yield returned +0.40% with spreads at 336 bps. Higher-rated bonds outperformed lower-rated ones. Leveraged loans returned +0.36% with spreads at 496 bps, and about 10% of loans traded above par versus 5% the prior week.
Preferreds rebounded sharply and returned +0.64% while stocks fell more than 4% on Thursday, helped by strong inflows and low dealer inventories.
Convertibles were the only major sector to decline, absorbing most of the equity drawdown. The Thursday equity selloff was tied to data center regulation fears and partly reversed Friday.
The 30-year conforming mortgage rate fell 15 bps on the week and is approaching 7%. The MBS index returned 0.57% with spreads at 30 bps.
Global emerging market index returned +0.31% with spreads at 196 bps. Local-currency bonds led, with South Africa, Brazil and Colombia ahead.

Equity volatility tied to data center regulation fears.
Heavy issuance of bonds from large technology and AI-linked companies.
Weaker borrowers in high yield and leveraged loans are underperforming higher-quality issuers.

geopolitical: An energy shock is cited as the main variable for core inflation and the Fed path.
U.S. midterm election results are cited as a driver of safe-haven buying in Treasuries and of tighter investment grade spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong payrolls and hawkish Fed officials support one more hike by year-end, which Nuveen expects, followed by an extended hold through 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Treasuries rallied for a fourth week despite payrolls more than doubling expectations, as investors sought safety after the election and focused on equity weakness rather than the jobs data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The energy shock's pass-through to core inflation, which Nuveen says determines the path. U.S. CPI on 10 November is the next data point.
